questions.prompt: Why do you square each distance from the mean instead of adding the plain distances?
options: Squaring makes the result smaller and easier to read
The plain distances always add up to 0, so they cannot measure spread
Squaring removes the unit, so lists in different units can be compared
The plain distances are always positive already
questions.explanation: Numbers above the mean balance numbers below it, so plain distances sum to 0. Squares are all positive and cannot cancel.

questions.prompt: The numbers 4, 6, 4, 6 have a mean of 5. What is their standard deviation, dividing by the count?
questions.explanation: Each distance is 1 or -1, each square is 1, the mean of the squares (the variance) is 1, and the square root of 1 is 1.

questions.prompt: Route A has a variance of 2 minutes squared. Why do you take the square root at the end?
options: To put the answer back in minutes, the unit of the original numbers
To make the answer always smaller than the mean
To correct for having only 5 mornings of data
To turn the answer into a percentage
questions.explanation: The variance is in minutes squared because the distances were squared. Its square root, 1.41 minutes, is in the same unit as the times.
